description: Is the internet up at each site, how long were the outages, and how much data was used and by whom. Outages come from the internet-probe poller on rpi5 (home), skullsaints (blr) and ubuntu-dev (homelab); usage comes from the ER605, OPNsense, the hypervisor and the Bangalore TP-Link router.

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. 1 means no probe round failed in the last 15 s (a sliding window, so a blip between two scrapes still shows for a while); 0 means at least one round did not reach the internet (no TCP or DNS target answered). It does not say whether the failure was local or upstream; see Current outage and the Outages table.
panels.title: Internet now

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. 1 - downtime / range length, from confirmed outages only (2 failed rounds in a row, about 10 s). Blips are not counted. If the poller started part way into the range, the whole range is still the denominator, so the figure is slightly optimistic. Capped by Prometheus retention (7 days).
panels.title: Availability over the range

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. Confirmed outages (2 or more failed rounds in a row) that started in the range, rounded. Brief blips of one round are not included. Counter comes from the poller's ledger, so it survives restarts.
panels.title: Outages in range

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. Seconds of confirmed outage in the range, including the outage that is still open. Blips are not included.
panels.title: Downtime in range

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. How long the open outage has lasted. 0 means no outage is open. Does not include blips or past outages.
panels.title: Current outage

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. Time since the latest closed outage ended (read it as '... ago'). Empty if the host has no closed outage on record. The ledger keeps every outage; run internet-probe.py --report outages for the full history.
panels.title: Last outage ended

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. How long the latest closed outage lasted, and whether it was local (the site's own router did not answer) or upstream (the router answered, the internet did not).
panels.title: Last outage duration

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. Age of the poller's last write. Red over 60 s means the poller or the host's Alloy has stopped, so every other panel here is stale. Cannot tell you about an outage of the monitoring path itself (a site that is offline cannot report).
panels.title: Probe freshness

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* from the internet-probe poller on each site's host (rpi5 = home, skullsaints = blr, ubuntu-dev = homelab), written every 15 s. One value per selected site. Whether the poller can write its on-host outage ledger (SQLite, the permanent record). Ledger error means outage history and the outage counters may be incomplete; fix the host's disk or the data directory.
panels.title: Ledger

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_up (0 when a round failed in the last 15 s), lowest value in each interval so a short outage is not averaged away. Red is a failed round, not necessarily a confirmed outage (needs 2 in a row). Gaps mean no data: the poller or host was off.
panels.title: Internet up or down

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_gateway_up, the site's default gateway (a TCP connect that succeeds or is refused counts as up). Down here while the internet is down means a local fault (cause=local); up means the router answered and the fault is upstream. Does not test Wi-Fi or any device behind the router.
panels.title: Gateway up or down

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_down_seconds_total, confirmed outage seconds per day (blips excluded). Days are the Grafana step, not local midnight. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.
panels.title: Downtime per day

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_outages_total, confirmed outages that started per day, rounded (blips excluded). The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days; the Loki table below goes back 30.
panels.title: Outages per day

panels.description: Source: the internet-probe journal lines in Loki (30 days), one per closed outage, filtered by the selected sites. Fields are the labels that `| logfmt` extracts from the line. closed_by=restart means the poller restarted during the outage, so the end is the restart time, not the real recovery. Outages still open appear only in the logs panel below. Older history: internet-probe.py --report outages on the host.
panels.title: Outages

panels.description: Source: the internet-probe journal lines in Loki (30 days): outage_start (a confirmed outage began), outage_end, and blip (fewer than 2 failed rounds, no ledger entry). Filtered by the selected sites. One line per event, no per-round noise.
panels.title: Outage events and blips

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_target_rtt_seconds, the last round's connect (tcp), reply (dns) or request (http) time per target and site. A target that failed in that round has no point. Measures the path from the site's host, not from your devices.
panels.title: Round-trip time per target

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_gateway_rtt_seconds, TCP connect time to the site's default gateway. Omitted while the gateway is down. A high or spiky value here with a normal internet RTT points at the local network.
panels.title: Gateway round-trip time

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_failed_rounds_total / internet_probe_rounds_total, five-minute rate. A round fails only when no tcp or dns target answered. Counters restart from zero when the poller restarts; rate() handles that.
panels.title: Failed-round ratio

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_target_failures_total, five-minute rate times 60. A single target failing while the others answer is not an outage: that is how a flaky resolver or one provider shows up. Includes the informational http target.
panels.title: Target failures per minute

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total on the ER605's WAN port (role=wan), read over SNMPv3: direction in is download, out is upload. This is the whole household's internet use, but it does not say which device. Bits per second, five-minute average.
panels.title: Download and upload rate

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total{role=wan,direction=in}, increase over the time range. Whole household, from the ER605 WAN port; includes the homelab (OPNsense sits behind the ER605). The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.
panels.title: Downloaded in range

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total{role=wan,direction=out}, increase over the time range. Whole household, from the ER605 WAN port; includes the homelab. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.
panels.title: Uploaded in range

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total on the ER605 WAN port, increase per day. Whole household including the homelab. Days are the Grafana step, not local midnight.
panels.title: Daily usage

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total on the ER605 WAN port, increase per hour. Whole household including the homelab.
panels.title: Hourly usage

panels.description: Source: er605_if_octets_total{role="wan"} joined to er605_wan_info on interface, increase per day per ER605 WAN. With one WAN, or before the poller exports er605_wan_info, everything is wan1.

targets.expr: sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[1d]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[1d])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[1d]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[1d])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

panels.title: Daily usage per WAN

panels.description: Download and upload over the range for each ER605 WAN (er605_if_octets_total{role="wan"} joined to er605_wan_info on interface). The household total is the stat above.

targets.expr: sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[$__range]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[$__range])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[$__range]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[$__range])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

panels.title: Household usage per WAN, in range

panels.description: Sent plus received over the range. Home internet: er605_if_octets_total on the ER605 WAN port (whole household, homelab included). Homelab: opnsense_interfaces_*_bytes_total on the OPNsense WAN interface. CAVEAT: OPNsense WAN also carries traffic between the home LAN and the homelab (for example Plex to a Mac at home), so the homelab figure is an upper bound on its internet use, and ER605 minus OPNsense is NOT the household's share.
panels.title: Homelab vs home internet, in range

panels.description: Source: opnsense_interfaces_received_bytes_total plus transmitted, per OPNsense segment, increase over the range. Counts everything the firewall routed for that segment, including traffic between segments and to the home LAN, not only internet. Traffic between two guests on the same segment never reaches the firewall and is not counted (Guest Traffic sees it).
panels.title: Homelab segments, in range

panels.description: Source: opnsense_interfaces_received_bytes_total (traffic the segment's hosts sent into the firewall) and opnsense_interfaces_transmitted_bytes_total (traffic the firewall delivered to the segment), per segment, increase over the range. Same caveats as the bar gauge: not only internet, and no same-segment guest-to-guest traffic.
panels.title: Homelab segments table

panels.description: Source: the hypervisor's receive counter on each guest NIC (tap/veth), named by fleet_pve_guest_nic_info, the same query as Guest Traffic's Most Data Sent. Counts ALL guest traffic (to other guests, to the LAN and to the internet), not only internet use. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, sum by (guest, nic) (sum_over_time((increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) ((topk by (host, device) (1, timestamp(fleet_pve_guest_nic_info))) > bool 0))[$__range:5m]))))

panels.title: Top 10 guests, sent in range

panels.description: Source: the hypervisor's transmit counter on each guest NIC (tap/veth), named by fleet_pve_guest_nic_info, the same query as Guest Traffic's Most Data Received. Counts ALL guest traffic, not only internet use. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, sum by (guest, nic) (sum_over_time((increase(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) ((topk by (host, device) (1, timestamp(fleet_pve_guest_nic_info))) > bool 0))[$__range:5m]))))

panels.title: Top 10 guests, received in range

panels.description: Source: tplink_router_wifi_client_bytes_total from the TP-Link Archer C5 poller on skullsaints (Bangalore site), increase over the range per Wi-Fi client. Wi-Fi clients only: wired devices and traffic the router forwards in hardware are not counted. Same query as Router TPLink Blr.
panels.title: Blr usage per client, in range

panels.description: Source: tplink_router_wifi_client_bytes_total from the Archer C5 poller on skullsaints, increase per day per Wi-Fi client (download plus upload). Wi-Fi clients only. Same query as Router TPLink Blr.
panels.title: Blr daily usage per client

panels.description: Explains what this dashboard cannot attribute to a device, and the OPNsense WAN caveat. No query.

options.content:
### Per-device usage at home is not available yet

The ER605 forwards most traffic in hardware, so its own per-IP statistics see only about 4% of it. A **per-device** breakdown of the **home** network needs the planned port mirror of the ER605 LAN ports to t7920 `nic0`, with a flow counter attributing each byte to a device. See [Routers and firewall](https://harshitruwali.github.io/homelab-infra/monitoring/monitoring/routers/#er605-home-router).

Until then, home usage is a single household total (the ER605 panels above). Per-device figures exist for the Bangalore site (Wi-Fi clients, from the TP-Link router) and for homelab guests (from the hypervisor).

### Reading the homelab numbers

- **OPNsense WAN is not a clean internet counter.** It also carries traffic between the home LAN and the homelab (for example Plex to a Mac at home), so it is an upper bound on the homelab's internet use.
- **ER605 WAN minus OPNsense WAN is not the household's share.** The two overlap and the difference includes that LAN-to-homelab traffic.
- **Per-guest bars count all traffic**, not only internet, and per-segment figures count what the firewall routed, not only internet.

panels.title: What is not measured

panels.description: 1 - downtime / observed time per site, from the monthly sums. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site AS metric, availability AS value FROM net.monthly_internet WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Availability per month

panels.description: Confirmed internet outage seconds per site (blips excluded). Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site AS metric, down_seconds AS value FROM net.monthly_internet WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Downtime per month

panels.description: Confirmed internet outages per site. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site AS metric, outages AS value FROM net.monthly_internet WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Outages per month

panels.description: ER605 WAN bytes, all WANs. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, 'download' AS metric, download_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE wan = 'total' AND month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date UNION ALL SELECT month::timestamp, 'upload', upload_bytes FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE wan = 'total' AND month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Household download and upload per month

panels.description: Download plus upload per ER605 WAN. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, wan AS metric, total_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND wan <> 'total' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Household usage per WAN per month

panels.description: Bytes routed per OPNsense segment (received plus transmitted). Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, interface AS metric, total_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_segment WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Bytes per segment per month

panels.description: The five guests with the most traffic in each of the last six months. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month, guest, sent_bytes, received_bytes, total_bytes FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY total_bytes DESC) AS rn FROM net.monthly_guest WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '5 months')::date) t WHERE rn <= 5 ORDER BY month DESC, total_bytes DESC

panels.title: Top 5 guests per month

panels.description: Every closed internet, per-WAN path and ER605 WAN outage, newest first (last 500), kept forever. closed_by restart means the end is the poller restart time. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT started_at AS "Start", ended_at AS "End", site AS "Site", kind AS "Kind", name AS "Name", target AS "Target", duration_seconds AS duration_seconds, cause AS "Cause", closed_by AS "Closed by" FROM net.outage_events WHERE kind IN ('internet', 'path', 'wan') ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: Outage history (permanent)

title: Internet and Usage
